title: Fresh recovery incarnation and signing-key epoch
description: Objective: mint the non-restored fencing identity that every disaster restore must install. Deliverable: a daemon recovery-incarnation service using the production Node crypto boundary to create a 256-bit CSPRNG nonce and a fresh signing-key epoch, bind both to one backup-generation digest and restore command ID, and return only verification-safe metadata plus protected key material handles. MEASURED GAP at HEAD 1ce0059: RestoreQuiesceWitness carries an arbitrary `recoveryIncarnationRef`, but repo-wide searches find no recovery-incarnation mint, `keyEpoch`, entropy health gate, or restore-key rotation service. NOT in scope: incrementing restored counters, two-slot file installation, session/grant validation, effect inventory, R3 approval, fault fixtures, or persisting raw private keys in events/logs. Hard dependency: task-5606947a9d7d4f228dc63e6ce4dea69a defines the backup-generation digest it binds; implementation may plan in parallel but cannot complete against a guessed contract. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-incarnation.* and minimal daemon export wiring. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: The production service obtains exactly 32 bytes from a CSPRNG and generates a new signing-key epoch outside restored state, returning a frozen versioned binding over restoreCommandId, backupGenerationDigest, incarnation digest/reference, key-epoch reference, and verification-key fingerprint.

Two distinct restore command IDs for the identical backup generation produce distinct incarnation and key-epoch references; no counter, timestamp, backup byte, or caller-selected ID can supply either fresh identity.

Entropy failure, short/randomly repeated output, key-generation failure, or unverifiable public-key metadata refuses with stable `RECOVERY_ENTROPY_UNAVAILABLE` or `RECOVERY_KEY_EPOCH_UNAVAILABLE` at layer `RECOVERY_INCARNATION`, truth `UNKNOWN`, and no prepared authority.

Tests exercise the production crypto adapter, assert no private-key bytes appear in serialized outcomes/errors, pin exact refusal code/layer precedence, and mutation-check the production freshness comparison.

Private signing material must remain behind an OS/protected-key port and must not enter events, manifests, errors, logs, tests, or evidence.
Tests for refusals assert exact stable reason code and `RECOVERY_INCARNATION` layer.

implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED landed and verified red for the RIGHT reason.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run ... src/recovery/recovery-incarnation.test.ts` -> exit 1, **63 failed / 2 passed (65)**. Every failure is `createRecoveryIncarnationService is not a function` / `createNodeRecoveryCryptoPort is not a function` — the expected missing-public-symbol failure, not a broken test file.

The 2 passing cases are deliberate and are the rail's anti-vacuity guards: they assert the generated matrices actually generated cases (`INVALID_REQUESTS.length === 21`, `ENTROPY_FAULTS.length === 7`, `KEY_FAULTS.length === 12`) and touch no missing symbol. A sweep that silently produced zero rows would fail these BEFORE any behaviour is asserted.

WHAT IS SPECIFIED (65 cases)
- Vocabulary: exactly three closed codes in precedence order, frozen; schema version literal; `RecoveryIncarnationErrorCode` and the result union pinned with `expectTypeOf` against the production constants.
- Request admission (21 rows + 2): every row asserts `calls.order` is EMPTY — the ordering claim is that nothing reached the CSPRNG, not merely that it refused. Covers missing/extra keys, the four forbidden caller-supplied identity fields (nonce, keyEpoch, counter, timestamp) plus incarnationRef, non-string/empty/over-long/control-char/non-NFC command IDs, and uppercase/63/65/non-hex/non-string digests. Accessor-backed request refused outright; a separate case mutates the request object AFTER `mint()` returns its promise and proves the binding still carries the pre-await snapshot.
- Real Node adapter path: full binding shape, every reference `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`, 128-hex Ed25519 signature, 88-hex (44-byte) SPKI, deep freeze; exactly 32 bytes requested from the CSPRNG; two commands over ONE generation get distinct incarnation ref, incarnation digest, key-epoch ref, key fingerprint and binding digest; identical retry does not remint (randomBytes called once); rebinding one command to a second generation refuses; two concurrent identical mints collapse to one minting.
- Fault matrix (19 rows): 7 entropy (throw, reject, non-Uint8Array, string, 31 bytes, 33 bytes, null) each asserting `generated === 0` so entropy is proven before a key exists; 12 key (throw, reject, null, wrong algorithm, non-Uint8Array SPKI, empty SPKI, non-object handle, sign throw, sign non-Uint8Array, verify throw, verify false, verify truthy-non-boolean) each asserting the CSPRNG was still asked for exactly 32. Every row goes through `expectRefusal`, which pins code AND layer `RECOVERY_INCARNATION` AND `truth: "UNKNOWN"` AND `authority: "NONE"` AND the absence of `binding`/`keyHandle`.
- Freshness proven on RAW material: a repeated CSPRNG block is refused even when BOTH the command and the generation differ — the derived reference would differ, so only a comparison on the raw block can catch it. Same shape for a repeated public key. Plus burning (a block reserved on an attempt that later died at the key leg is still refused later) and a simultaneous-claim case where exactly one of two concurrent commands may take a repeated block.
- Precedence: malformed + dead CSPRNG -> INPUT_INVALID with an empty call order; short entropy + dead key generation -> ENTROPY_UNAVAILABLE with `generated === 0`.
- Leak checks: a `SENTINEL` string is thrown from every one of the 19 fault legs and asserted absent from the serialized refusal. A recursive walker over `Reflect.ownKeys` (so NON-enumerable properties are included) forbids functions, Error, ArrayBuffer, any ArrayBuffer view, `CryptoKey`, the raw nonce hex, and any string matching /private|secret|pkcs8|seed/i. `keyHandle` is asserted non-enumerable and absent from `JSON.stringify`.
- Adapter-level protection: a fabricated `{}` handle and a `structuredClone` of a real handle both fail to sign, a destroyed handle stops signing, the handle serializes as `{}`, and the exported SPKI round-trips through `importKey`.

DELIBERATE TEST-DESIGN CHOICES WORTH REVIEWING
1. The stub port's DEFAULT legs are real WebCrypto Ed25519, not fakes; only the named fault row replaces a leg. A green row therefore cannot pass by never having touched real crypto.
2. Two cases recompute `sha256(domain || bytes)` independently and compare to the published digest. That is deliberate duplication of a one-line derivation, used as an oracle for "the raw block was hashed, not published" — it is not a reimplementation of the service's logic.
3. `expect(node instanceof webcrypto.CryptoKey)` rather than a name check, so a renamed class cannot slip through.

Node facts measured on THIS machine (v24.16.0), not assumed: `subtle.generateKey({name:'Ed25519'}, false, ['sign','verify'])` gives a private key with `extractable:false`, `type:'private'`, `usages:['sign']`; SPKI is 44 bytes; signatures are 64 bytes; verify succeeds. `@moe/store` is already a declared `@moe/daemon` dependency, so importing the digest TYPE adds no manifest change.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the recovery-incarnation contract and stateful mint service. Import only the type `BackupGenerationManifest['generationDigest']` from @moe/store; defensively snapshot the exact request synchronously before the first await and validate canonical NFC bounded command ID plus lowercase hex64 digest. Define immutable request/binding/proof/success/refusal/opaque-handle/crypto-port types, schema and error constants, fixed no-secret refusal factories, and domain-separated canonical hashing. Maintain per-service in-flight/success bindings by restore command so concurrent or repeated identical command+digest calls reuse one mint while rebinding the command to another generation refuses. Request exactly 32 entropy bytes, hash and reserve the raw block before any key await, refuse repeats independently of command context, then derive the context-bound incarnation reference; after key generation, fingerprint and reserve the complete canonical SPKI before self-proof, derive the key-epoch/binding digests, sign and verify the exact canonical challenge through the port, and return only a deep-frozen `MINTED`/authority-NONE result whose protected handle is frozen and non-enumerable. Burn seen values on later failure, best-effort destroy candidate handles, never return caught diagnostics, and preserve the primary stable code if cleanup also fails.

Implement the production Node crypto adapter in a separate focused module. Use Node 24 WebCrypto/getRandomValues or randomBytes for the requested 32 bytes and `subtle.generateKey({name:'Ed25519'}, false, ['sign','verify'])`; require a private CryptoKey with type private, extractable false and signing usage, retain it only in a module-private WeakMap keyed by a frozen empty opaque handle, and export only the public key's canonical full SPKI DER. Re-import/round-trip the SPKI, require Ed25519 public metadata, implement Ed25519 sign and public verify for the service's challenge, and delete the handle on destroy; a structured clone or fabricated handle must not resolve to a key. Re-export only the reviewed `createNodeRecoveryCryptoPort` value from the public recovery-incarnation barrel, and add exact one-line bridges so the existing raw-Node bridge/loadability gate covers both modules.

Publish the minimal reviewed surface and drive tests GREEN. comments.content: SPIDR/title warning adjudication: nonce and signing-key epoch remain one task because the design requires one atomic fresh fencing identity; landing either alone would create an installable half-authority. Composition consumers are task-b6e3dd2af916490fb2bc4d375a530683, task-8a01c025b65246aca09e69d82e009587, and task-6f786c58cabf4f85be8ed4135e68a752.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Use a stateful daemon mint service plus an injected protected-key crypto port. The default Node 24 adapter uses WebCrypto Ed25519 with a non-extractable private CryptoKey retained only in an adapter-private WeakMap; it returns a frozen empty opaque handle, canonical public SPKI metadata, and a self-verified binding proof. Rejected classic KeyObject because it is structured-cloneable and its private PKCS8 bytes remain exportable even though JSON.stringify misleadingly yields {}; rejected raw/private key bytes, PEM/PKCS8 outcomes, counter/time/restored-state derivation, caller nonce/key-epoch fields, and hashing only the backup/command. Raw 32-byte entropy fingerprints and full canonical SPKI fingerprints are compared and reserved independently before context-bound references are derived, so changing restoreCommandId or backupGenerationDigest cannot mask a repeated CSPRNG block or key. Add a distinct RECOVERY_INCARNATION_INPUT_INVALID code rather than mislabel malformed/hostile input as entropy or key failure. The service accepts the committed @moe/store BackupGenerationManifest['generationDigest'] type and validates lowercase hex64, but returns MINTED with authority NONE; it does not reimplement or claim BackupGeneration verification. RecoveryAnchor alone owns PREPARED/INSTALLED.

planningNotes.risks: A non-extractable WebCrypto CryptoKey hidden behind a WeakMap handle is protected against caller export but is process-volatile, not an OS-durable keystore reference. This task must state that limitation and must not claim crash-resume persistence or PREPARED authority; RecoveryAnchor/controller must later supply an OS-protected durable key provider before CORE-S14 can pass. Snapshot the exact request before the first await; reject proxies/accessors/extras and caller nonce/key/counter/time. Async simultaneous mints require atomic in-flight command binding plus synchronous reservation of raw entropy fingerprints before key generation and key fingerprints before proof verification; same command+digest reuses the in-process mint, while the same command rebound to another generation refuses. Burn suspect fingerprints even when later stages fail. Full SPKI DER, not a tail slice, is fingerprinted and round-tripped; sign/verify the canonical domain-separated binding challenge before returning. Every port throw/false/malformed value maps to a frozen constant refusal, cleanup failure never replaces the primary code, and no caught message/Error, Buffer/view, CryptoKey/KeyObject, function, raw nonce, or private-shaped field may escape. Keep both production sources <=250 and the root index <=250, preserve foreign work, and stage only the seven named paths.
